chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) wrote to me:

Say in the prostration of gratitude one hundred times: 'Thanks, thanks' or, if you wish, 'Forgive, forgive.' The author of this book said: Sulayman ibn Hafs met Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) and al-Ridha (peace be upon him) both, and I do not know from which of the two this report is.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (a title for Imam al-Ridha or Imam Musa ibn Ja'far)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dhikr for the prostration of gratitude according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This tradition highlights the Shia emphasis on *sajdat al-shukr* (prostration of gratitude) as a distinct act of worship, with the Imam instructing Sulayman ibn Hafs to recite 'Shukran' or 'Afwan' one hundred times. The compiler’s note on the uncertainty between Imam Musa ibn Ja'far and Imam al-Rida reflects the common scholarly practice of attributing teachings to the broader Ahl al-Bayt lineage when specific transmission chains overlap. This practice underscores the spiritual discipline of constant gratitude and seeking divine pardon as intertwined aspects of devotion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-23 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd, on the authority of Soleiman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, “Abul Hassan (s) wrote me a letter in which he (s) wrote,

Say ‘Thanks Thanks’ or ‘Forgive Forgive’ one hundred times when you perform the prostration for expression of your gratitude.”The author of this book (Sheikh Sadooq) said, “Soleiman ibn Hafs visited both Musa ibn Ja’far (s) and Al-Ridha (s) and I do not know from which of the two Imams (s) this tradition has been narrated on the authority of.”
